sections.text: This procedure outline the steps required to change spacers on 500kv over head transmission line, bundle conductor using Russian telescoping truck.

items:
Obtain an authorized 
 work permit
The set - up location for the telescope truck must be level
Local temporary earthing must be installed on both sides of the work location
Flash glasses, Safety Helmut
Safety boots, Gloves

rows: Telescopic tower truck capable of extending to 26 meters
Steel conductor cleaning brush with universal fitting
Insulated operating stick with universal fitting

items:
Climb the towers on both sides of the work location using approved fall 
 arrest procedures and maintaining the minimum limits of approach to the 
 conductor

Check the circuit to ensure isolation 
 using a potential tester.

Install temporary earthing cables 
 according to approved earthing procedures
The work supervisor shall determine the appropriate location to set up the telescopic truck to change the spacer.
Lower and fix the jacks of the telescopic truck to ensure stability.
The line worker climbs into the basket with the tool bag and replacement spacers.

Raise the telescope ensuring that that the vertical axis of the telescope tower does not deviate greater than 3 degrees from vertical according to the angle indicator on the
 truck
The basket is raised to a suitable height to enable the line worker to work comfortably on the conductor.
The old spacer is then removed from the conductor.
The conductor must be cleaned with a metal brush at the position where the spacer was originally installed.
Install the new spacer on the cleaned conductor and tighten completely.
After finishing the work, the telescopic tower is lowered and the line worker descends from the basket.
Lower the jacks of the truck and prepare to move.
Remove the temporary earthing cables from both adjacent towers and lower to the ground.

Complete the work order to connect the line in accordance with
 EEC Electrical Safety Rules.

Transmission Lines | Technical Procedure
Introduction
This procedure outline the steps required to change spacers on 500kv over head transmission line, bundle conductor using Russian telescoping truck.
Safety Precautions
Obtain an authorized 
 work permit
The set - up location for the telescope truck must be level
Local temporary earthing must be installed on both sides of the work location
Tools and Equipment
Flash glasses, Safety Helmut
Safety boots, Gloves
Qty | Item
1 | Telescopic tower truck capable of extending to 26 meters
1 | Tool bag
1 | Clamp stick
2 | Earthing cables
1 | Steel conductor cleaning brush with universal fitting
1 | Insulated operating stick with universal fitting
1 | Potential Tester / Voltage Indicator
1 | Insulating Gloves
1 | Flash glasses for each worker
Work to be Carried Out
Climb the towers on both sides of the work location using approved fall 
 arrest procedures and maintaining the minimum limits of approach to the 
 conductor
Check the circuit to ensure isolation 
 using a potential tester.
Install temporary earthing cables 
 according to approved earthing procedures
The work supervisor shall determine the appropriate location to set up the telescopic truck to change the spacer.
Lower and fix the jacks of the telescopic truck to ensure stability.
The line worker climbs into the basket with the tool bag and replacement spacers.
Raise the telescope ensuring that that the vertical axis of the telescope tower does not deviate greater than 3 degrees from vertical according to the angle indicator on the
 truck
The basket is raised to a suitable height to enable the line worker to work comfortably on the conductor.
The old spacer is then removed from the conductor.
The conductor must be cleaned with a metal brush at the position where the spacer was originally installed.
Install the new spacer on the cleaned conductor and tighten completely.
After finishing the work, the telescopic tower is lowered and the line worker descends from the basket.
Lower the jacks of the truck and prepare to move.
Remove the temporary earthing cables from both adjacent towers and lower to the ground.
Complete the work order to connect the line in accordance with
 EEC Electrical Safety Rules.
